description: A peer-reviewed conference paper (full, short or workshop): page-limited and judged quickly.
section: Conference Paper, Short Paper, Workshop Paper, and Extended Abstract
goal: Make the paper ready for submission: clear contribution, convincing evidence, calibrated claims, within the venue's limits.
note: Judge the paper as a whole under the page limit: the first page must make the problem, contribution and evidence clear; respect anonymization if the review is double-anonymous.

readers.persona: a time-pressed program-committee reviewer who must decide within about twenty minutes whether the paper is clearly novel, sound and well evaluated; reports the first doubts that would lower the score and whether the contributions are believable from the abstract, introduction and main results

a researcher who knows the field well; flags what is imprecise, outdated, shallow or missing (assumptions, guarantees, recent results, failure cases, open problems, key related work) and anything they would skip as already known
a busy reader who reads only the title, abstract, headings, first sentences, figures, captions, tables and conclusion; flags when the contribution, method and evidence cannot be recovered that way

reviewers.focus: correctness of every definition, claim, derivation, equation, algorithm, number and code fragment; recompute numerical examples with a script; consistent notation, units and dimensions; correct statements of known results and their assumptions

calibration and coherence of claims: no overclaiming (unsupported superlatives, 'prove' for empirical results, 'state of the art' without dated evidence, generalizing beyond the evidence) and no underselling (stacked hedges, buried or vague contributions); every contribution stated in the abstract and introduction is supported by specific evidence in the body and restated consistently in the discussion and conclusion; limitations are honest, specific and stated once, in one compact Limitations subsection, with only a brief qualifier where a claim depends on them; no evidence-level tags or audit labels on claims in the running text; numbers and claims agree everywhere they appear

experimental design and reporting: research questions mapped to experiments, appropriate datasets and baselines (strong, tuned, current), ablations, statistical uncertainty (seeds, variance, confidence intervals, significance where claimed), fair comparison and compute budgets, reproducibility details, negative or mixed results reported, and conclusions drawn only from what the experiments show

novelty and significance relative to the closest prior work: what is new, why it matters, whether the related work section positions the contribution accurately and fairly, and whether the paper explains what the reader can now do that they could not before

every reference is real and correctly described: verify authors, title, venue, year and identifier (DOI, arXiv id, ISBN or publisher page) with web search and the citation checker; flag any reference that cannot be found as a blocker; check that each cited work actually supports the sentence citing it, that primary sources are cited, and that essential related work is not missing

the rendered document: figures, tables, equations, algorithms, lists, headings and layout; legibility at print size, labels and units, captions that say what to notice, every figure and table referred to and explained in the text; render the pages and look: floats near their first mention, no clutter and no large blank areas; the paper reads as a research narrative (problem, idea, method, implementation, case study or evaluation, results, discussion), each section opening with what it does and how it follows from the previous one, and no section repeating another

fluency, coherence and readability: paragraph flow and transitions, one idea per paragraph, each fact, caveat and definition said once (a short pointer elsewhere, no paragraph repeating another, within or across sections), narrative rather than ledger wording (no 'committed', 'archived', 'recorded run' or evidence-level tags in the running text; provenance stated once), short clear sentences with jargon explained at first use for a reader from a neighboring field, consistent terminology, no repetitive wording or formulaic transitions, the house rules (no en or em dashes, only needed hyphens, no comma right after a conjunction or connective, no paragraph opening with 'To', every abbreviation written out at first use and none in the abstract, no internal identifiers such as function names, versions or hashes), no chains of 'and', parallel lists, sentence variety, concision, and American or British spelling used consistently as configured

compliance with the venue's or call's requirements: page or word limits, template and formatting, anonymization for double-anonymous review, required sections and statements (limitations, ethics, broader impact, reproducibility or data availability checklists, funding, conflicts), reference style and supplementary material rules

editors.focus: prose: clarity, concision, flow between sentences and paragraphs, terminology, punctuation including hyphens and dashes, parallel lists; remove filler, formulaic transitions and repetition without removing substance or adding claims

notation, terminology and spelling across the document and against the glossary; numbers, names and claims identical wherever repeated (abstract, introduction, body, conclusion); labels, cross-references, captions, citation and reference formatting
